Research snapshot: 28 September 2026
Public contracts + dated research + an original reference design

An end-to-end learning path through mapmaking, imagery, places, routing, navigation, geospatial intelligence and operations. Independent educational work; not an official Google publication or a certified navigation system.

How to use this playbook

This book develops Meridian, a fictional mapmaking and geospatial platform. A source reports a changed road, an accepted edition becomes searchable and navigable, and a traveler receives a route that must remain consistent with current constraints. The same architecture extends to places, imagery, transit, fleet tools, private location sharing and grounded assistance.

The recurring distinction: an observation, an accepted fact, a published artifact, a predicted journey and current permission are different records. Reliability requires preserving those differences through updates, retries, failover and restoration.

Four kinds of evidence

Public contractOfficial product documentation, API behavior, standards and service commitments. Geography, access stage, billing and dates matter.
Dated disclosureMaps research explains specific mechanisms. Broader Google infrastructure papers are not a complete current Maps service topology.
Reference designThe service boundaries, schemas, algorithms and operating targets for Meridian are original design proposals, not private Google internals.
Local experiment98 passing local tests and deterministic synthetic experiments. These demonstrate selected properties, not field accuracy or navigation safety.

Choose a learning route

Architecture: Chapters 1-6 and 55-66. Maps and location: Chapters 7-18. Routing and navigation: Chapters 19-33. Places and personal experiences: Chapters 34-48. Developer platform: Chapters 49-54. Failure walkthroughs: Chapters 67-72.

Each chapter begins with a concrete question and an evidence-and-scope panel. Diagrams connect the components, while design checkpoints expose failure cases. The appendices connect the narrative to data records, contracts, algorithms, tests and reproducible experiments.

Production scope

The book does not claim access to private source code, current ranking weights or every internal service. API availability is not route correctness, and a route is not a guarantee of physical safety. Verify current provider agreements, source rights, feature access and geographic coverage before deployment.

Part 01 / Chapters 01-06

Foundations: a model of the changing world

Follow the world model, current constraints and evidence boundaries.

Chapter 01

The product atlas: more than a map on a screen

What must a company build before a blue dot becomes a useful journey?

Google Maps Platform exposes distinct map, route, place, navigation, environment and analytics products. Consumer Maps additionally has experiences such as Ask Maps and Immersive Navigation, whose March 2026 announcement specifies rollout scope rather than universal availability. [S1] [S2]

Start with the job, not the technology

A traveler wants to find an entrance, choose a way there, understand uncertainty and arrive. A shop owner wants customers to find accurate information. A city wants to understand recurring congestion. A developer wants a predictable interface, permission to use the returned content and an intelligible bill. These jobs overlap in geography but differ in authority, latency and acceptable error.

This book designs Meridian, a fictional Maps-like company. Its first market is a bounded metropolitan area with licensed road data, participating transit agencies and reviewed place records. Meridian is not an implementation of Google's private source code. It is a concrete reference design against which the public evidence can be understood.

Divide the platform into five responsibilities

The world-model plane ingests imagery, partner feeds, observations and corrections. It resolves disagreements and publishes immutable editions. The decision plane searches places, calculates routes, predicts traffic and estimates arrival time. The experience plane renders maps, guides navigation, handles offline operation and exposes uncertainty. The personal-data plane owns saves, sharing, history and consent. The platform plane controls API credentials, quotas, commercial contracts and metering.

Keep physical-world records separate from personal records. A road restriction belongs to the road model; a member's route history is not a public road fact. A business claim is evidence to evaluate, not an unrestricted write to every search result. A model score recommends an alternative; it cannot silently authorize a prohibited vehicle movement.

A journey is a composition of services

Consider a person looking for a cafe before a train. Discovery retrieves candidates, checks current place status and supplies entrances. Walking routing uses the pedestrian graph rather than a car-road projection. Transit planning uses a service date, transfer constraints and fresh disruption evidence. Navigation tracks progress without treating every noisy location point as an actual turn. Each answer should identify what is known, what is predicted and what remains uncertain.

The same coordinates can name a building centroid, driveway, loading bay, transit platform or accessible entrance. A useful product preserves that distinction through its APIs. Converting everything into one latitude/longitude pair loses the very information needed for arrival.

What to launch first

Start with reliable search, road routing, a usable client and a correction operation. Add live traffic only where observations and evaluation support it. Add advanced modes after collecting their constraints, not by changing an icon on a driving route. A small high-quality map is a better foundation than global coverage with unmeasured errors.

A product coverage register records geography, mode, device, data license, maturity, freshness and responsible team. It prevents a sales page, an experimental feature and a generally available API from becoming one accidental promise.

Design checkpoint

For every feature, name the authoritative record, its update source, its expiry policy and the user-visible fallback. If these cannot be stated, the feature is not yet an operational service.

Chapter 02

Public engineering history and evidence boundaries

Which parts of the architecture are actually public?

Google has published Maps-specific work on mapmaking, traffic prediction, road partitioning, routing preferences and transit transfer patterns. Colossus publications describe a shared storage foundation, but do not reveal the complete Maps service topology. [S5] [S19] [S20] [S26] [S77]

Read architecture as a dated claim

A technical article answers a question in the context of its publication. A 2010 transit paper can establish that a transfer-pattern approach accelerated Maps queries then; it does not prove that every present-day transit request follows that implementation. A 2023 routing account is strong evidence for the described preference-learning technique, not a license to invent the surrounding databases and RPC graph.

The book uses four evidence classes. Public contracts define documented API behavior and applicable commitments. Maps-specific disclosures explain a component at a point in time. General research supplies algorithms or infrastructure concepts. Reference design is Meridian's proposed implementation, justified by requirements rather than attributed to Google.

An engineering timeline worth learning

The useful progression is conceptual: transit routing reduced query work through precomputation; mapmaking combined heterogeneous evidence; visual positioning improved localization where satellite positioning was unreliable; graph-based prediction incorporated neighboring traffic; learned route preferences captured choices beyond shortest travel time; newer experiences combined these capabilities with conversational interfaces.

Do not turn this sequence into a monolithic technology stack. Traffic modeling, image reconstruction, road graph publication and device navigation can evolve independently. An accurate overview describes the boundaries between them, including compatibility contracts and update rates.

What remains non-public

This study does not know the complete current service map, all database schemas, current shard counts, private routing code, model weights, network placement, fraud thresholds or internal latency budgets. The following chapters provide explicit proposed alternatives where those details are needed to build a company. An uncertainty label is useful engineering information: it tells the reader which assumptions require validation.

For example, choosing a transactional database for map-release pointers is a design decision. Naming Spanner as the only possible implementation would be unjustified. Similarly, S2 is a public geometric library, while using its cell IDs as the primary partition key for every Maps dataset would be an unsupported extrapolation.

Keep an evidence ledger

For each important statement, record the source, publication date, product scope and whether the claim concerns a research prototype, production deployment or public API. Record the date on which living documentation was checked. Pin a source snapshot in the internal research process without redistributing copyrighted articles in the source bundle.

When sources appear to conflict, look for differences in time, region, surface and terminology first. Consumer navigation may expose a capability that the developer routing API does not. A limited-customer feature may be generally available in one region and experimental in another. The discrepancy is often a scope difference, not evidence that one source is wrong.

Apply the same discipline to your company

Publish service contracts that are narrower than marketing ambition. Maintain architecture decisions with the alternatives considered and conditions that would trigger a revisit. Never convert a local benchmark into a global production guarantee. The companion experiments in this book measure only their synthetic inputs and local implementations.

Chapter 03

High-level architecture from capture to arrival

How do offline map production and online routing cooperate?

The public mapmaking account describes combining imagery, authoritative data and user contributions. Routes and map-tile APIs expose different serving responsibilities. The architecture below is an original separation of those concerns, not a disclosed Google internal diagram. [S5] [S11] [S31]

Make slow work produce fast, verifiable inputs

Meridian has a production pipeline and several serving paths. The production pipeline ingests source bundles, validates coordinate systems and licenses, extracts candidate changes, reconciles identities, reviews high-risk edits and builds map editions. Each edition includes compatible road topology, turn restrictions, place links, renderable geometry and index artifacts.

An edition manifest names content hashes and schema versions. A transactional publication pointer makes a validated edition eligible for serving. Servers load it before advertising readiness. Publication does not copy the world into a database transaction; it atomically changes a small authoritative reference to already durable artifacts.

Separate the three online paths

A map-view request retrieves style, geometry and imagery appropriate to the viewport and device. A route request obtains a graph edition, applicable restrictions, traffic estimates and user constraints, then searches and validates alternatives. A place request retrieves structured entities and text/vector candidates, applies freshness and eligibility checks, and returns displayable details with attribution.

These paths share identities and geometry but should not share all failure dependencies. Losing a personalized recommendation model should not prevent basic route calculation. Losing a new imagery tile should not invalidate a road restriction. A route that cannot establish current closure information should not be presented with an unqualified live status.

The live overlay lane

Closures, incidents, traffic, elevator outages and transit updates arrive faster than base-map rebuilds. Keep them in bounded, versioned overlays with event time, validity interval, source confidence and expiry. Overlays refer to stable entities and the geometry edition against which matching occurred. A migration table maps old segment identities to replacement segments when roads split or merge.

A query context pins an edition bundle and records the live-overlay watermark it examined. Before returning a candidate, a final validator checks critical constraints again. A revocation arriving during computation may force a retry or a safe no-route result. Perfect knowledge of the physical world is impossible; bounded internal freshness is still enforceable.

Data and control ownership

The map publisher owns edition activation. The closure service owns current restriction decisions. The routing service owns computed answers, not road truth. The navigation session owns which answer is currently guiding the client. Personal sharing permissions live in an independent service. Each owner emits a durable event through an outbox so dependent systems can update without controlling the original transaction.

Keep deployment simple until scale demands more

An initial region can use a relational control store, object storage, a spatial database, a queue and memory-resident route graphs. Large deployments split ingestion by geography, route serving by graph partitions, and personal records by account. Sharding should follow access patterns and recovery boundaries, not the desire to draw many boxes.

Review question

Can the system serve an older map safely while a new edition is building? The answer must mention compatibility, critical overlays, expiry and user-visible freshness, not merely caching.

Back to contents
Chapter 04

Domain model, identities and non-negotiable invariants

What must remain true when observations and indexes disagree?

Place IDs can change, and Google recommends refreshing older stored IDs. Spherical cells, rendering tiles and business identities serve different purposes. Meridian therefore treats identifiers, geometry and revisions as separate concepts. [S7] [S9] [S43]

Model entities before tables

A road segment is a directed traversable connection, not just a polyline. A turn joins directed segments under mode and time constraints. A place is an entity with claims, categories, entrances and lifecycle state. An observation is evidence about one of these entities. A map edition is a reproducible set of accepted revisions. A route is a decision over a specified edition and conditions.

Use opaque stable internal IDs for entities and immutable IDs for revisions. Coordinates are attributes, not primary keys. Two shops can occupy the same coordinate; a shop can move; a road can be redrawn without changing its real-world identity. Splits and merges need explicit lineage, not an update that silently repurposes the old ID.

Separate the clocks

Store at least source event time, observed-at time, ingestion time and effective interval where applicable. A closure reported at 10:05 may have started at 10:00. A feed arriving at 10:10 is not necessarily newer evidence than one ingested at 10:08. Clock quality itself is metadata. Compare revisions using a source sequence when available, rather than trusting arbitrary device timestamps.

Five invariants

A published manifest references complete, validated artifacts. A stale publisher cannot activate a release after losing its epoch. A route marked valid against a restriction snapshot contains no edge forbidden by that snapshot. A revoked sharing grant cannot authorize subsequent server disclosure. A deleted personal record cannot be restored to active use merely because an old backup contains it.

These are system invariants, not promises that all roads are physically safe. The world may change before an authoritative report arrives. The client must retain uncertainty and driver responsibility rather than letting a database constraint imply omniscience.

A practical record shape

A proposed road revision contains segment_id, revision, geometry_ref, from_node, to_node, mode_mask, restriction_ref, source_set, valid_from, valid_to and quality_state. A route result contains route_id, request_hash, graph_edition, overlay_watermark, cost_model_version, departure_time, steps, warnings and expires_at.

Do not put sensitive member identifiers into public map IDs, tile paths or telemetry keys. Distinguish project identity used for API billing from the person's identity used for saved places or sharing.

Consistency by responsibility

Use strong transactions for publication pointers, permission changes and deduplicated commands. Derived search indexes and tile caches may lag, provided they apply current restrictions at serving boundaries. Counters and aggregate analytics can be eventually consistent with explicit correction paths. Traffic estimates are versioned observations, not serializable financial balances.

Design checkpoint

Choose a single real-world change, such as one road becoming two. Enumerate every affected reference: turns, cached routes, observations, tiles, traffic bins, place entrances and offline bundles. If any consumer cannot tell which geometry its identifier denotes, the migration contract is incomplete.

Back to contents
Chapter 05

SLAs, SLOs and the meaning of a successful map

What does 99.9% availability actually promise?

The reviewed Maps Platform SLA commits to at least 99.9% monthly uptime for each Covered Service, using valid requests and server-side failures. It is not a consumer Maps promise, a route-safety guarantee or a traffic-freshness guarantee. Pre-GA and other exclusions apply. [S4]

Read the denominator first

The contractual calculation is request-based: successful eligible requests divided by eligible requests, with the contract defining failure. A chart of unavailable minutes is not that calculation. Ten thousand failed requests during a busy minute can matter more than a quiet outage of the same duration. Preserve per-project, per-service request evidence and the applicable exclusions.

The reviewed credit schedule is 10% below 99.9% but at least 99%, 25% below 99% but at least 95%, and 50% below 95%, subject to the agreement and claim requirements. Credits are not automatic compensation for every downstream harm. Recheck the current contract before relying on these terms. [S4]

Design objectives for Meridian

Set separate objectives for API availability, useful answers, latency, data freshness and recovery. Illustrative internal targets might be 99.95% successful eligible route requests, p95 simple-city routing below 500 ms, p99 below 1.5 seconds, and a p99 accepted emergency-closure propagation budget of 30 seconds in a covered region. These are proposed targets to test, not Google measurements or promises.

A useful-answer SLI distinguishes no feasible route from infrastructure failure. An accessibility query may correctly return no confirmed path. Returning a fabricated accessible route to improve success rate is worse than honestly reporting insufficient evidence.

Measure the physical-world gap

Maintain audited samples of road connectivity, entrance accuracy, restriction correctness, transit transfer feasibility and arrival-time calibration. Break metrics down by region, mode, time, device and data age. A global average can hide a dangerous failure for a small vehicle class or rural area.

For ETA, use absolute error, signed bias and interval coverage. A 90% prediction interval should be checked for approximately 90% empirical coverage in meaningful slices. A narrow interval with poor coverage is misleading even if its median error looks attractive.

Recovery objectives are dataset-specific

Base-map artifacts can often be replicated before activation. A release pointer should not advance unless recovery regions possess the referenced artifacts. Permission revocation and confirmed restrictions require much tighter loss bounds than recreatable analytics. Offline devices cannot satisfy an online freshness objective; expose their capability and last-sync time.

Define recovery-time objectives by a tested scenario: losing one serving zone, one region, a storage quorum or a corrupt edition. Include capacity restoration and cache warming, not only process startup. A database that has recovered while navigation uses incompatible graph versions is not a recovered product.

Error budgets with safety guardrails

Use availability budgets to slow risky releases when reliability deteriorates. Do not permit a budget tradeoff that knowingly violates hard restrictions or access control. Traffic quality, safety-related validation and privacy have independent launch gates. A green uptime dashboard cannot waive them.

Design checkpoint

Write one SLI that can detect a successful HTTP response containing a stale closure decision. That metric is necessary because an HTTP-only SLA will not detect the problem.

Chapter 06

Acquisition, licensing and the map operations company

Where does the map come from, and who can change it?

Google describes mapmaking as a combination of imagery, authoritative sources, local contributions and machine learning. Developer content-use and attribution rules are product- and contract-specific; access to an API is not permission to copy its data into a competing global map. [S5] [S67]

Data acquisition is a product dependency

Meridian needs licensed base roads, administrative geometry, transit schedules, addresses and place information before it needs a sophisticated neural ranker. Establish contracts with agencies, imagery providers and businesses. Record permitted uses, retention, derivative rights, attribution, geographic scope and termination obligations for every source. Legal review is part of onboarding, not a footnote after ingestion.

Do not bootstrap the company by scraping proprietary map tiles or republishing restricted API content. Open datasets also have licenses and attribution requirements. Keep independently sourced data and licensed third-party content separable so a contract change does not force an untraceable full rebuild.

Every source becomes an evidence stream

An ingestion envelope contains source identity, source revision, checksum, coordinate reference system, timestamps, geometry bounds, license label and transformation lineage. Validate files in a sandbox. Reject impossible coordinate ranges, duplicate sequence numbers with different content, malformed geometry and unexpectedly large geographic changes.

A successful import means the file is understood, not that its claims are accepted. A government closure feed, owner edit and imagery-derived road candidate carry different kinds of evidence. Store the claims separately before adjudication. This makes reversals and audits possible.

Review risk, not just confidence

Automate low-risk formatting corrections when evidence agrees. Escalate changes affecting road direction, bridge clearance, controlled access, accessible entrances or ownership disputes. A high-confidence visual detector can still confuse an overpass with an intersection; confidence is conditional on a model and training distribution.

Build an editor with before/after geometry, source overlays, affected routes and dependency counts. Two-person review for high-impact restrictions reduces unilateral mistakes. Reviewers need local context and language expertise, not merely a generic annotation interface.

Close the feedback loop

Allow users and partners to report errors with location, time and evidence. Issue a case ID, preserve the decision history and explain disposition where appropriate. Prioritize reports by potential harm, reach and corroboration. Never let report volume alone establish truth: coordinated abuse can manufacture volume.

Map operations should own backlog age, confirmed-error repair time and retraction quality. Measure how often a correction introduces a regression elsewhere. A merge that fixes search but breaks entrance routing is not a complete fix.

Plan the economics

Acquisition, refresh, review and dispute handling are recurring costs. A startup can rent infrastructure, but it cannot instantly rent trusted local knowledge in every jurisdiction. Expand geographically only when source quality, operational coverage and support are ready. The software architecture must make partial coverage explicit rather than pretending that missing attributes are permissive defaults.

Design checkpoint

A provider terminates a license. Can you find and remove all affected imagery, derived features and cached bundles while preserving independently sourced roads? The answer requires lineage and a deletion workflow, not a text search for the provider's name.
